708	// CreateAdjustment registers a quota adjustment against an entitlement. The
709	// caller-supplied adjustmentID is unique per entitlement: resubmitting it
710	// with the same delta and effective time returns the original adjustment
711	// without touching quota again (created=false); resubmitting it with a
712	// different delta or effective time fails without changing state. The
713	// adjustment is recorded as pending and folds into the quota total once its
714	// effective time has arrived — immediately when the effective time is not in
715	// the future. An increase always applies; a decrease applies only while the
716	// adjusted total still covers used plus unsettled quota, otherwise it stays
717	// pending and takes effect automatically once occupancy allows. A decrease
718	// that would drop the current quota total to zero or below fails and writes
719	// nothing.
720	func (s *Store) CreateAdjustment(ctx context.Context, entitlementID, adjustmentID string, delta int64, effectiveAt time.Time) (Adjustment, bool, error) {
721		if err := validIdentifier("adjustment_id", adjustmentID); err != nil {
722			return Adjustment{}, false, err
723		}
724		if delta == 0 {
725			return Adjustment{}, false, fail(CodeInvalidRequest, "delta is required and must be a non-zero integer")
726		}
727		if effectiveAt.IsZero() {
728			return Adjustment{}, false, fail(CodeInvalidRequest, "effective_at is required (an RFC 3339 timestamp)")
729		}
730		effectiveAt = effectiveAt.UTC()
731		tx, err := s.pool.Begin(ctx)
732		if err != nil {
733			return Adjustment{}, false, fmt.Errorf("begin transaction: %w", err)
734		}
735		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback(ctx) }()
736	
737		ent, err := lockEntitlement(ctx, tx, entitlementID)
738		if err != nil {
739			return Adjustment{}, false, err
740		}
741		// Fold in adjustments that came due earlier so a new decrease is checked
742		// against the current quota total.
743		if err := applyDueAdjustments(ctx, tx, &ent, entitlementID); err != nil {
744			return Adjustment{}, false, err
745		}
746	
747		var existing Adjustment
748		err = tx.QueryRow(ctx, `
749	SELECT adjustment_id, delta, effective_at, applied_at, created_at
750	FROM adjustments WHERE entitlement_id = $1 AND adjustment_id = $2`,
751			entitlementID, adjustmentID).
752			Scan(&existing.AdjustmentID, &existing.Delta, &existing.EffectiveAt, &existing.AppliedAt, &existing.CreatedAt)
753		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, pgx.ErrNoRows) {
754			return Adjustment{}, false, fmt.Errorf("load adjustment: %w", err)
755		}
756		if err == nil {
757			if existing.Delta != delta || !existing.EffectiveAt.Equal(effectiveAt) {
758				return Adjustment{}, false, fail(CodeAdjustmentParamChanged,
759					"adjustment %q already exists with delta %d and effective_at %s, not delta %d and effective_at %s",
760					adjustmentID, existing.Delta, existing.EffectiveAt.Format(time.RFC3339),
761					delta, effectiveAt.Format(time.RFC3339))
762			}
763			existing.Status = adjustmentStatus(existing.AppliedAt)
764			return existing, false, tx.Commit(ctx)
765		}
766	
767		if delta < 0 && ent.quotaTotal+delta <= 0 {
768			return Adjustment{}, false, fail(CodeInsufficientQuota,
769				"decrease of %d would drop the quota total of %d to zero or below", -delta, ent.quotaTotal)
770		}
771		var created Adjustment
772		err = tx.QueryRow(ctx, `
773	INSERT INTO adjustments (entitlement_id, adjustment_id, delta, effective_at)
774	VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
775	RETURNING adjustment_id, delta, effective_at, applied_at, created_at`,
776			entitlementID, adjustmentID, delta, effectiveAt).
777			Scan(&created.AdjustmentID, &created.Delta, &created.EffectiveAt, &created.AppliedAt, &created.CreatedAt)
778		if err != nil {
779			return Adjustment{}, false, fmt.Errorf("insert adjustment: %w", err)
780		}
781		// An effective time that has already arrived applies within the same

input.new_string:
### Expiry closure and the close-time snapshot

An entitlement is created in normal state. Once its `valid_to` has passed it is **closed exactly once, lazily and in the touching transaction**: the next write or view query on that entitlement stamps `closed_at` with the real time of that touch and registers one accounting record. A repeated touch never produces a second record or moves the close time. Closure is one-way — even if a reschedule later moves the entitlement back into a window covering the current time, it stays closed.

At closure the service writes a **closure snapshot**, keyed by the entitlement identifier (unique within the entitlement), capturing the actual figures at that instant: `seats_total`, `quota_total`, `used_amount`, the unsettled `reserved_amount`, `available_amount`, the `valid_from`/`valid_to` in force and `closed_at`. Due quota adjustments are folded in first, so the snapshot reflects the state really in force. The snapshot is a frozen record: later settlements change the live figures but never rewrite the snapshot.

Once closed, an entitlement rejects new reservations, quota adjustments, seat adjustments, reschedules and pause/resume registrations — each such request fails as a whole with 409 `entitlement_closed` and writes nothing. In-flight reservations can still be confirmed or released, confirmed reservations can still be corrected with a reversal, and an idempotent replay of a reservation, adjustment, reschedule or seat adjustment created before closure still returns its original record (200) without applying anything again.

`status` in the view is `closed` after closure; before closure it stays the window-relative `pending`/`active`/`expired`. Note the distinction: `expired` is a window label (a reschedule can move an entitlement from expired back to active), while `closed` is the permanent lifecycle state.

### Pause and resume issuance

Within the validity period, operations can suspend and resume grant issuance with caller-supplied business identifiers and times. Pause and resume never change any quota figure, seat figure or the validity window.

`POST /entitlements/{entitlement_id}/pauses`

```json
{"pause_id":"freeze-2026-0031","paused_at":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"}
```

`POST /entitlements/{entitlement_id}/resumes`

```json
{"resume_id":"unfreeze-2026-0031","resumed_at":"2026-06-03T00:00:00Z"}
```

`pause_id`/`resume_id` use the same character rules as the other business identifiers. They are unique within the entitlement and share one namespace across the two kinds (a single identifier denotes one event, either a pause or a resume). The first submission returns 201; resubmitting the same identifier with the same kind and time returns 200 with the original record and does not take effect again; resubmitting it with a different kind or time fails with 409 `pause_resume_param_mismatch` and changes nothing.

Time rules (validated strictly, so a bad time fails with 400 `invalid_request` and writes nothing): the pause time must be no earlier than `valid_from` and no later than `valid_to` (both bounds inclusive); the resume time must be strictly later than the matching pause time and no later than `valid_to`. Pausing an already-paused entitlement fails with 409 `entitlement_already_paused`; resuming one that is not paused fails with 409 `entitlement_not_paused`; registering either event on a closed entitlement fails with 409 `entitlement_closed` (apart from an identical replay). Pausing or resuming an unknown entitlement fails with 404 `entitlement_not_found`.

While paused, new reservations are refused with 422 `entitlement_paused`. Confirmation and release of in-flight reservations and corrective reversals are unaffected by a pause; quota and seat adjustments are not issuance and remain allowed. After a resume, new reservations are accepted again, and a fresh pause is then permitted.

Each reservation entry reports its business identifier, owning `department_id`, amount, lifecycle status (`pending`, `confirmed`, `released` for reservations; `reversed` for corrective reversals) and settlement timestamp. `used_amount` is confirmed quota minus effective reversals, so a reversed reservation leaves the original confirmation and the reversal both visible while the quota figures reflect only the net effect. Each adjustment entry reports its business identifier, delta, effective time and whether it is `pending` or `applied`; `quota_total`, `available_amount` and the other figures count only applied adjustments, so they always match the quota actually in force. Each reschedule entry reports its business identifier, the new start and end of the validity window, and its creation time, listed in creation order; the view's top-level `valid_from`, `valid_to` and `status` always reflect the latest reschedule that has taken effect. Each seat adjustment entry reports its business identifier, the seat delta, its creation time and `seat_total`, the cumulative seat total after that adjustment — deltas summed in creation order on top of the entitlement's initial seats; the list is ordered by creation time. Seat adjustments move only `seats_total`, never any quota figure.

173	
174	| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
175	| --- | --- | --- |
176	| `invalid_request` | 400 | Missing or illegal parameters, malformed JSON |
177	| `entitlement_exists` | 409 | Entitlement identifier already in use |

181	| `reservation_not_found` | 404 | Unknown reservation |
182	| `reservation_param_mismatch` | 409 | Business identifier reused with different parameters |
183	| `reservation_already_settled` | 409 | Reservation was already confirmed or released |
184	| `reservation_not_confirmed` | 422 | Reservation is not confirmed, so it cannot be reversed |
185	| `reservation_already_reversed` | 409 | Reservation was already reversed |
186	| `adjustment_param_mismatch` | 409 | Adjustment identifier reused with a different delta or effective time |
187	| `reschedule_param_mismatch` | 409 | Reschedule identifier reused with a different new start or new end |
188	| `seat_adjustment_param_mismatch` | 409 | Seat adjustment identifier reused with a different delta |

191	
192	Concurrent reservations, confirmations, releases, reversals, adjustments, reschedules and seat adjustments on the same entitlement are serialized with a row lock in PostgreSQL, so used quota plus unsettled reservations never exceeds the total quota, the seat total never drops below the seats allocated to departments, repeated requests never grant, refund, adjust quota, rewrite the validity window or move the seat total twice, and failed requests leave no partial results. Due quota adjustments are folded into the quota total inside the same lock — by whichever operation or query touches the entitlement first after the effective time — so every adjustment applies exactly once and a decrease never crowds out occupied quota. Each seat adjustment entry reports its business identifier, the seat delta, its creation time and `seat_total`, the cumulative seat total after that adjustment — deltas summed in creation order on top of the entitlement's initial seats; the list is ordered by creation time. Expiry closure happens in that same lock, on the first write or view after `valid_to`: it stamps one `closed_at` and inserts one closure snapshot atomically, so concurrent or repeated touches close it exactly once, the snapshot reads the figures actually in force at that instant, and the close either fully happens or not at all. Closure, pause and resume serialize with reservations, settlements, reversals, adjustments, reschedules and seat adjustments on the same row lock; pause and resume change only the pause flag and append their event records, never a quota figure, seat figure or the window, and failed requests leave no partial results. # closed_at set, and closure_snapshot freezes seats/quota/used/reserved/available.

# Live figures moved (used/reserved now 0), but closure_snapshot still shows the

curl -s 127.0.0.1:8080/entitlements/team-omega

content.text:
Done. I extended the Go/PostgreSQL entitlement service with one-way expiry closure (with a close-time snapshot) and caller-timed pause/resume, serializing everything on the existing per-entitlement row lock. All unit and integration tests pass (including `-race`, and repeated runs), and I verified the flows live over HTTP including a restart.

## What changed

**Domain (`internal/entitlements/entitlements.go`)**
- Schema (auto-migrated, additive): `entitlements.closed_at`, `entitlements.paused_at`; new `closure_snapshots` table (PK = entitlement id → at most one) and `pause_resume_events` table (unique `(entitlement_id, event_id)`, ordered by creation).
- `closeIfDue` runs on **every touch** inside the same tx/lock: once `valid_to` has passed and it isn't already closed, it folds due quota adjustments, then atomically inserts the snapshot and stamps `closed_at` with the real `now()` — exactly once (idempotent by PK + guarded update). Snapshot freezes seats/quota/used/unsettled-reserved/available, the window and close time; later settlements move live figures but never rewrite it.
- Closed entitlements reject **new** reservations, adjustments, seat adjustments, reschedules, pauses, resumes with `entitlement_closed` (409), writing nothing. Idempotent replays of pre-close records still return 200 originals; in-flight confirm/release and confirmed-reservation reversals stay allowed. Closure is one-way — a reschedule back into an open window is still refused.
- `PauseEntitlement`/`ResumeEntitlement` with shared, per-entitlement idempotency: same id+kind+time → original record (200); different kind/time → `pause_resume_param_mismatch` (409). Pause time ∈ `[valid_from, valid_to]`, resume time > matching pause and ≤ `valid_to` (else 400); pause-while-paused `entitlement_already_paused` (409), resume-while-not-paused `entitlement_not_paused` (409), paused new-reservation `entitlement_paused` (422). Settlement/reversal unaffected while paused; no figure or window changes.
- View adds `status: "closed"`, `closed_at`, `closure_snapshot` (omitted when open) and `pause_resume_events` (id/type/at in registration order).

**HTTP (`internal/httpapi/handler.go`)**: `POST /entitlements/{id}/pauses` (`pause_id`,`paused_at`) and `/resumes` (`resume_id`,`resumed_at`), strict JSON, same envelope, new codes mapped; health endpoints untouched.

**Tests/README**: added closure/snapshot/one-way/concurrency/restart and full pause/resume integration tests, HTTP route tests, updated affected pre-existing tests for the new semantics, and documented both features with curl walkthroughs.

## Run / verify (project convention)
```sh
go test ./...                                   # unit (integration skips w/o DB)
mkdir -p .local
initdb -D .local/pgdata --auth=trust --encoding=UTF8 --locale=C
pg_ctl -D .local/pgdata -l .local/postgres.log -o '-h 127.0.0.1 -p 15432' -w start
createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 15432 entitlements
TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://127.0.0.1:15432/entitlements?sslmode=disable' go test ./...
DATABASE_URL='postgres://127.0.0.1:15432/entitlements?sslmode=disable' LISTEN_ADDR=127.0.0.1:8080 go run ./cmd/server
```
Then follow the new "Verifying expiry closure and the snapshot" and "Verifying pause and resume" sections in the README. (For my verification I used an isolated cluster on port 15611, since 15432/15433 were already occupied; I stopped it afterward.)

One design decision worth flagging: pause/resume share a single id namespace (`event_id` unique across kinds), so reusing a pause id for a resume is a `pause_resume_param_mismatch` — matching "同一标识…参数不一致". Say the word if you'd rather allow the same string independently per kind.
